background_process_management: Four target enumerations (INV-1 mean; INV-7 p_fail; INV-8 d_reg; INV-7 p_exist) were run SEQUENTIALLY (never concurrently, unlike RUN-RELN-141a86-stage0bcde's three-way-parallel jobs) via run_stage0c_repair_monitor.py, which launches each as its own subprocess.Popen and polls that subprocess's real /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 2.0 seconds from the parent (monitor) process, writing every sample to memory-timeseries-<target>.json. Each worker also carries its own INTERNAL soft cap (11.0 GB / 5400 s, checked only between complexity levels -- see implementation note in execution-report.md on why this internal check did not fire promptly for large levels), and the external monitor enforces a HARD backstop (13.0 GB / 6000 s) independent of the worker's own check, via SIGTERM then (after a 3s grace period) SIGKILL. All four targets were terminated by the external monitor's 6000-second wall-clock hard cap (none reached the 13 GB memory hard cap, though INV-8 came within 0.19 GB of it); this is recorded, per target, in memory-timeseries-<target>.json and target-enumeration-raw-results.json.
